Becoming one of the biggest movie stars in the world was only the beginning for Willis in the summer of 1988. He and then-wife Demi Moore would welcome Rumer, the first of their three daughters, when she was born Aug. 16. Willis and current wife Emma Heming Willis also share two daughters.
Before he officially became a girl dad for the first time, Willis told Gumbel he was “anxious” about Rumer’s arrival and admitted he couldn’t grasp how much his world was going to change.
“I keep thinking that nothing can prepare you for that, you know, that it’s just, no matter how wild you think it is, that it’s gonna be 10 times that,” he said.
Willis, who has kept a lower profile since being diagnosed with frontotemporal dementia in 2023 following a 2022 aphasia diagnosis, also had a good sense that he was entering uncharted territory.
“I really think that no matter how well I can get ready for it, we’re going to make mistakes. Parents make mistakes, I think. I don’t think anybody can really do it perfectly,” he said.

title: Prince George Turns 13! See Proud Parents Prince William and Kate Middleton Celebrate the Teenager
summary: Prince George is now a teenager and turned 13 on July 22. Read his parents sweet post celebrating the milestone birthday.
story: Prince George is now a teenager!
Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales, celebrated Prince George’s milestone 13th birthday with a sweet message on their official Instagram account Wednesday, July 22.

“Happy 13th Birthday, George! 🎉” they captioned a photo of their oldest child, decked out in a dark blazer, pants and white button-down shirt. In the new portrait, he sports a slight smile with his hands in his pockets.

The couple also shared a video of George on a beach playing with his younger brother, petting his dog and swinging a cricket bat, with the caption, “Thank you for all the birthday wishes for George today!”
The royal couple are also parents to Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, 8.

The former Kate Middleton and her husband reveal special family photos of their children every year to mark their birthdays. Last year for the now-teen’s special day, the Prince and Princess of Wales’ official Instagram account shared a video of the three siblings holding hands. Prince George and Princess Charlotte also carried their younger brother and laughed in the clip.

The family recently attended the Men’s 2026 Wimbledon Final on July 12. Prince William, Kate, George and Charlotte sat in the Royal Box as they watched World No. 1 Jannik Sinner defend his title and secure the championship trophy for the second year in a row. Prince Louis did not attend the event.

After his win, Sinner was seen chatting with the family. In a video shared on ESPN’s YouTube page, the star athlete asked the children if they practice tennis every day. George and Charlotte shared that they usually practice on the weekends.

Shortly after the final, the Prince and Princess of Wales shared a congratulatory post on Instagram, featuring a video of the family cheering at the event. George appeared almost as tall as mom Kate in the footage.
“A brilliant Men’s Final at The Championships. Congratulations @janniksin on a superb performance and a well-earned @wimbledon title!” the caption read.

Prince George’s 13th birthday comes after a Kensington Palace spokesperson confirmed to NBC News in June that he is set to follow in his father’s footsteps and attend Eton College starting in September.

Eton College is a private boarding school in Windsor, England, that was founded in 1440 by King Henry VI. In addition to Prince William, former British Prime Ministers Robert Walpole, David Cameron and Boris Johnson studied there, as well as uncle Prince Harry and great-uncle Earl Charles Spencer.

title: I’m a ‘Love Island USA’ Fanatic. Here’s What to Watch Next to Fill the Void
summary: What shows are like Love Island USA? Here are the shows and specific seasons to watch now that Love Island USA season 8 is over.
story: Take it From Me is a TODAY.com series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this latest installment, “Love Island USA” superfans share their top reality shows that will have viewers hooked all summer long.
“Love Island USA” has officially come to an end, which means fans now have six-days worth of free time they need to fill.

Season 8 of the hit Peacock series wrapped July 12, with Bryce Alakai and Trinity Tatum being named the winners. But with that happy, romantic ending came the sad realization that it will be months until fans hear “I got a text,” watch contestants compete in a series of make out-filled challenges and witness intense recouplings.

Superfans Mike Gauyo (@blackboywrites), Adrianna (@adriannasmiles) and Kristi Cook (@spillsesh), who spent the last six weeks posting about the show on social media, racking up millions of views and likes, are also feeling the absence of “Love Island USA.”
So, they’ve shared with TODAY.com their recommendations on the next binge-worthy shows to keep reality television lovers busy the rest of the summer.
Read on for a list of specific shows and seasons that these superfans consider “must-see” television.
‘The Traitors’ Seasons 3 and 4
If you are looking for a show that has even more drama and a strategic element, then you might want to check out Peacock’s “The Traitors.”

The series brings together current reality television stars and legends, and places them in a Scottish castle. There, they compete as Faithfuls and Traitors. The Faithfuls must determine who among them are the Traitors, a group that secretly meets every night to plot their next murder. Every episode, a contestant is banished and must reveal their true identity. The series is packed with fun challenges and impressive game play, all culminating in a grand finale where one or multiple players win the cash prize.
Television writer and content creator Gauyo tells TODAY.com that “The Traitors” Season 4, which was released earlier this year, was his “all-time favorite” season of a reality television show.
“That season was must-see TV, especially the finale with Rob Rausch and Maura Higgins tête-à-tête for the prize money,” he says, referring to two stars of the “Love Island” franchise.

Content creator Adrianna agrees that “The Traitors” is one of the best reality television shows, highlighting Seasons 3 and 4 specifically. She described the series as her “favorite game of deception” thanks to a cast filled with “reality stars from all types of shows, from ‘Survivor’ to ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race’ to ‘Love Island.’”
“Think of ‘Clue’ meets ‘Knives Out’ meets ‘Show Me the Money,’” she continues. “It’s entertaining week after week because you never know who will be eliminated next.”
Those who already watched “The Traitors” have the civilian-only version to look forward to. Gauyo says he’ll be tuning in when “The Traitors: New Blood” premieres this fall on NBC on Sept. 17.
‘Big Brother’ Season 28
If you enjoy “Love Island USA” mostly because you get to see what the islanders are up to nearly every day (except hump day), then “Big Brother” might be the show for you.

The CBS staple kicked off its 28th season on July 9, introducing 14 new houseguests and three reality television icons. “Big Brother” airs three nights a week but fans can also watch all the alliances and backdoor plans form in real-time thanks to the show’s 24/7 live feeds. With the feeds, fans experience key moments, providing context that is sometimes missing from the show.
Gauyo recommends catching up on the current season since only a few episodes have aired.

Content creator Kristi Cook of Spill Sesh is a fan of the series, too. She notes the multiple episodes per week and the “addictive social dynamics and nonstop twists” of “Big Brother” will draw “Love Island USA” viewers in.
“The live feeds mean there’s almost always something to watch even when new episodes aren’t on,” she adds.
‘Love Island UK’ Seasons 12 and 13
If you are interested in checking out other versions of “Love Island,” you should start with the flagship UK series.
“For those who haven’t watched the UK version of Love Island, I highly recommend watching the last season that just aired. So good,” Gauyo praises.

Season 12, or “series” as they say across the pond, welcomed the first-ever American contestant to the UK version, which takes place at a villa in Mallorca, Spain. Toni Laites, the first bombshell of the season, was a server from Las Vegas who wasn’t afraid to ruffle feathers from the moment she arrived. The season also included many islanders who delivered captivating television, like Harry Cooksley, Shakira Khan and Helena Ford.
While the UK version is hosted by Maya Jama, it features comedian Iain Stirling as the narrator just like “Love Island USA.”
The current 13th season began June 1, the same week “Love Island USA” Season 8 premiered. However, the UK series runs for eight weeks, meaning the islanders are still in the villa.
Cook says she has already started Season 13 to fill the “Love Island USA” void.
“I couldn’t keep up with both it and Love Island USA at the same time, but now I finally have something to watch every day again,” she says.
‘Vanderpump Rules’ Seasons 1-7, and 9-10
If you want to take a break from reality competition shows but still want an unscripted series, “Vanderpump Rules” is a great option.

The show, which premiered on Bravo in 2013 and focuses on the staff at “The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills” alum Lisa Vanderpump’s restaurants and bars, launched the career of “Love Island USA” host Ariana Madix.
Adrianna shares with TODAY.com that “Vanderpump Rules” is “one of my favorite reality shows ever.”
“If you ever wondered where ‘Love Island USA’ host Ariana Madix got her start, she joins the cast in Season 2,’” she says.
Adrianna acknowledges that the show hits some low points around Season 7.
“But come back for Season 9 to get context before heading straight into ‘Scandoval’ in Season 10,” she says, referencing the major fallout between Madix and ex Tom Sandoval.

title: Beatriz Hatz Didn’t Wear Shorts Until She Was 17. Then She Went on ‘Love Island USA’
summary: Beatriz Hatz discusses her “Love Island USA” experience, hopes for future disability representation on reality TV and training for the Para National Championships.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.
“Love Island USA” Season 8 star Beatriz Hatz is a two-time Paralympian and Paralympic medalist. But unlike most elite athletes, the 25-year-old’s career started as “part of a joke.”
Hatz said on TODAY July 20 she first tried track and field in high school after a challenge from a friend.
“She was like, ‘You beat me at softball, basketball, I know what I can beat you at — track and field,’” Beatriz recalled.

At the time, she was using a walking prosthetic that weighed around five to seven pounds. She agreed to give the sport a chance anyway, motivated in part by the coveted title on the line: “Most Athletic in the Friend Group.”
Beatriz did far more than win the wager. She began competing in increasingly competitive meets, and eventually, she said, “unknowingly” qualified for the World Para Athletics Junior Championships.
“I got a call like, ‘Hey, do you want to represent Team USA?’” she said. “I was 17, and I was like ‘Oh yeah, sure.’”
The Colorado-raised athlete made her debut at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games and won bronze in the women’s 200 meter race at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.

But in June, Beatriz stepped onto a very different stage when she joined Season 8 of “Love Island USA” as a hopeful single. She explored connections with fellow OG islander Sean Reifel and Day 2 bombshell Gabriel Vasconcelos, and ultimately, made franchise history as the first contestant with a visible, physical disability.
On July 23, just weeks after the show wrapped with its July 12 finale, Beatriz is set to compete in the long jump at the Para National Championships in New York.

Speaking with TODAY.com before her interview with Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones, Beatriz opens up about dating with a disability, representing her disability on reality TV and catching up with her fellow islanders after the season finale. Plus, she shares about how she stayed in tip-top shape for her upcoming championship race while in the villa.
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.

They gave me free range of like, “OK, we’re willing to do what you’re comfortable with. We don’t want to make it a big deal because we chose you for you and not your leg.” Like, “Your leg has nothing to do with why you’re on the show. We really love you, your personality. We think you’re great. Now, like whatever you want to do, like if you want to walk in and act like it’s not a thing, then do that.” And that’s what I did.

I walked in and I was like, well, I don’t really have to say anything because at the end of the day, with all this small talk, it’s like, “Oh, what do you do for work?” And what do I do for work? I’m a professional track and field athlete for the Paralympics. And then it segues into, “Oh, I’m missing my leg.” I think they definitely showed my disability in a way of like “she’s very able to do anything.”

I think there’s a lot of stereotypes that come with disability. You think of somebody that is most likely older, very dependent on somebody else. Most of the time, not in a relationship, most of the time, probably not attractive. But just my existence does break those stigmas, and I think that’s what the world needs to see is that we’re not what you think we are. We’re just people.

Over the years, it’s changed a lot. I was very insecure when I was younger, so I actually didn’t wear shorts in public until I was 17 years old. That was my first time, and now I’m 25, so it’s still not that long ago.

This is probably my third or fourth year with the metal showing on my prosthetics, so it has evolved. When I go to the bar and stuff, and if I’m wearing like pants, it’s not the first thing I say to a guy. “Hey, by the way, I’m missing my leg.” Now if a conversation is going well then it’s like, “Oh, I’m a Paralympian. I do this and this. I’m an amputee,” just to kind of let them know, yeah, I am an amputee, but also I think everybody’s entitled to their preference. I don’t think it’s something to just like spring on somebody.
I took my blade with me. I actually did some training with my blade on. I know they didn’t show it, but I was training.

There’s that little grass patch, so there’s the fire pit, and then there’s all that grass. And I just did a bunch of long jump drills, like repetitive takeoffs, a lot of technical work in the blade, and I did like a tendon ligament circuit, just as much stuff as I could do. And anytime I was called to do something, I’d be running across the villa, just because I did kind of feel a little stir crazy. I was like, I can’t do an actual workout so I’m just gonna run around everywhere.

There was no way to fully keep up with the training the way that it should be done, because my training will take three to four hours, maybe on the track, depending on what we’re doing and how fast or slow we’re going about things. But in the villa, it’s like, you’ve got time to do this, and then you got to go back to doing your other things, like having chats. So I had to be very efficient with the work I was doing.

I have been able to catch up with quite a few of the islanders. I think I’m very excited to see where everybody’s career goes. I think everybody’s so deserving of the love that they’re receiving, and I wish everybody was receiving a lot more love.

The internet is a crazy place, and I don’t think anybody truly knows the islanders the way that we do. And I can’t even say that we know each other super well. Yeah, we spent the summer together, but I wasn’t there for the whole time, anyways. But nobody knows you the way your mom knows you, or your sister knows you, or your best friend knows you, right? And I think that’s something that a lot of people on the internet are forgetting. They think they know us because the TV show does an amazing job of making the viewers think they know you, when in reality, we are very much multifaceted people that have feelings, and I think that that’s one thing that’s missing.

I don’t think I was in a position to really give them advice because they’re definitely going to be in a bigger spotlight. Like they made it to the finals, and they do have a relationship walking out of this. So the only thing that I did give them was love.

Oh my gosh, my DMs are flooded with a bunch of amputees or Latinos or female athletes, and it is really cool to see all the communities that I have touched their hearts, and they’ve seen me on screen and felt that they can relate to me whether they have a disability or not. It’s really cool, but what really is super special to me is when I get messages from young girls that are amputees, and they’re like, “Wow, I’ve been struggling with this.” Or, “You’ve helped me with my confidence.” And those are the messages that I make sure to respond to because it’s like I really wish somebody would have been that for me.

I would just like to see more representation, period. I think people would look at me and would think, oh, she probably is shy or insecure about her leg. But then when I was on the show you could really see me, and people saw, oh, she’s funny, she’s outgoing, she’s doing all these challenges — and I think that’s perfect.

I think more people just need to be given the space and opportunity to even be on screen. I don’t think one person can represent the entire community because we are all different people, but I think it would be really cool to just see more people with disabilities, and especially different kinds. There’s so many disabilities that people don’t know about, and invisible ones at that. My best friend and roommate, she has cerebral palsy. She’s a Paralympian, but people will look at her and be like, “Oh, you’re not disabled.” But then, when you really look at the way like she runs, you’re like, “Oh yeah, you do have a disability.” And I think it’s just like the level of education around disability could definitely go up if there was more representation.

title: Malcolm-Jamal Warner’s Widow Sues His Mother, Successor Trustee, for $1.2 Million in Prenup Dispute
summary: Tenisha Warner, the widow of “The Cosby Show” star Malcolm-Jamal Warner, is suing the late actor’s mother for breach of contract involving the couple’s prenuptial agreement.
story: Tenisha Warner, the widow of “The Cosby Show” star Malcolm-Jamal Warner, is suing the late actor’s mother for breach of contract involving the couple’s prenuptial agreement.

NBC News obtained a copy of the complaint, confirming Tenisha Warner filed the lawsuit on July 20 in the Superior Court of Dekalb County in Georgia. The complaint names mother-in-law Pamela Warner as one of the defendants as she is the successor trustee of the Warner Family Trust. Tenisha Warner alleges in the  suit that she and Malcolm-Jamal Warner — who shared a 9-year-old daughter — married on May 23, 2022, and signed a premarital agreement eight days prior. The lawsuit says Malcolm-Jamal Warner did not fulfill the obligations in the prenup.
Tenisha Warner claims that her late husband “agreed to purchase and maintain a term life insurance policy on his life in the amount of $1,000,000,” with her as the “sole beneficiary.”

But she alleges that the deceased never purchased the life insurance policy for himself or one for her despite the agreement. The complaint also states that Malcom-Jamal Warner agreed to pay his wife $16,000 a year on their anniversary, create a retirement account and pay her a salary of $5,000 per month as his “chief of staff” but failed to do so.
The complaint claims that Tenisha Warner is owed “no less than $1,276,042.46,” plus interest and attorney’s fees and cost.

“Plaintiff performed all obligations required of her under the Agreement, including entering into and remaining in the marriage until the Decedent’s death,” the complaint reads. “The Decedent died without having satisfied his obligations under the Agreement, and no person or entity has paid or provided the sums due to Plaintiff under the Agreement.”

Pamela Warner has been the successor trustee of the Warner Family Trust since Oct. 7, 1996, the document states. The document also lists a “John Doe” as the second defendant because a personal representative has not been named for Malcom-Jamal Warner’s estate.

Additionally, according to the complaint, Tenisha Warner is requesting Pamela Warner, as  successor trustee, be prevented from “distributing, transferring, encumbering, or dissipating” trust property.

“For the last year, I have attempted to privately settle my beloved husband’s complicated estate and honor his last wishes,” Tenisha Warner said in a statement to People. “Malcolm had every intention to provide for our 9-year-old daughter and me. He was close to finalizing a new estate plan to replace the stale plan created in 1996 when he was 26 years old, 20 years before we met and well before we gave birth to our beautiful daughter.”
Tenisha Warner added that her late husband was “unable to do so before we lost him.”

“I have been struggling to care for our daughter as a single mom and now as her sole provider,” she continued. “Legally, I had no choice but to take action to protect our rights before any potential statute of limitations expired. We thank you for your support, love and understanding as we work through this painful process while honoring Malcolm’s life on the first anniversary of his death.”
Reps for Tenisha Warner, Pamela Warner and Malcolm-Jamal Warner’s estate did not immediately return TODAY.com’s request for comment.

Malcolm-Jamal Warner, best known for playing Theo Huxtable as a child star at the start of his decades-long career, died exactly one year before the suit on July 20, 2025, from an accidental drowning in Costa Rica. He was 54.

A representative of Costa Rica’s Judicial Investigation Agency shared a report at the time that said Malcolm-Jamal Warner was swimming at Playa Grande de Cocles when he “apparently was dragged by a current offshore.”
He was rescued and taken to shore where the Costa Rican Red Cross tried to revive him. He was pronounced dead at the scene.
On the anniversary of his death, Pamela Warner penned a letter to her son that was uploaded to his “living legacy” Instagram page.

The message included childhood photos of the “Malcolm & Eddie” star and said, in part, “As I look back, I have no regrets. Perhaps a little more time. Perhaps one more chance to cook his favorite meals, have one last good conversation, one last good deep belly laugh, the kind that produces those tears of pure joy, one last kiss, one last hug.”

She added, “One of the graces in all of this is that we had had healing conversations a few weeks before. We did not know that these were really good-bye conversations. There was nothing left unsaid between us. There was nothing ‘left on the table.’ And I believe that this is why I have been able to be at peace with Malcolm’s transition. I knew beyond a doubt that he loved me and more importantly trusted me. And he knew that I would love him forever and a day.”
Pamela Warner also said that in the past year she has “discovered how cruel, evil and greedy a human can be.”

title: Matt Damon Praises His Female Stunt Double in ‘The Odyssey’: ‘Had the Greatest Arms’
summary: Matt Damon praises his female stunt double that took his place during a vital scene in “The Odyssey.”
story: Matt Damon has called “The Odyssey” the “hardest” and most “challenging” movie he’s ever done, thankfully he had some help from his stunt double.

The 55-year-old actor stars in Christopher Nolan’s adaptation of Homer’s epic poem, which follows Odysseus’ grueling journey home after the Trojan War. Along the way, he encounters cyclops, giants and more supernatural beings, all which led to a physically strenuous performance for the actor.
Praised for his physical transformation during a recent interview, Damon took a moment to shine the light on his female stunt double, Devyn Dalton.

“When we did the force perspective stuff of the Laestrygonians... there were these stuntmen who were all 7 feet and then they got stuntmen who were under 5 feet,” Damon told Josh Horowitz on “Happy Sad and Confused” of the scene with the giants. “And so my double was a woman, a female stunt performer, who had the greatest arms I’ve ever seen.”
He recalled meeting Dalton for the first time at a catering tent and embracing her.

“I went up and I hugged her,” Damon said. “And I thanked her for all the work she’d put in.... And there are those shots in the movie where you see these giants looming over me... so it was almost 100% my arms in the movie, but gotta give it up where it’s due.”
In the comments section of Horowitz’s Instagram video, Dalton wrote that it was an “honour to double” for Damon.
In her own Instagram post documenting her personal epic journey as Odysseus, she called the gig “an adventure.”
“Scottish Highlands. The Odyssey. What an adventure. No spoilers just yet, but I’m incredibly grateful to be a part of the Laestrygonian battle,” she wrote.
She added that stunt doubling “the incredible” Damon was “an epic team effort.”

“We worked hard, shared plenty of laughs, and created memories I’ll never forget,” Dalton continued. “The best part of this job is getting to venture to new places and meet amazing people along the way.”
According to Dalton’s impressive IMDB, she is a Canadian born actor, dancer and stunt performer, as well as known for her motion capture performances.
Among her previous credits include “Rise of the Planet of the Apes” and “War for the Planet of the Apes,” “The BFG,” “Scary Movie,” “Descendants: Wicked Wonderland,” “The Last of Us” and many more.

Damon previously shared on Sunday Sitdown that the prep he had to do “as a guy in his 50s” for the film was its “own challenge.” Nolan cautioned him about the extremes that he and the entire “Odyssey” team would face.

“He was like, ‘This movie’s gonna be hard.’ And I looked at him like, ‘I’ve made, I don’t know 80 movies,’” Damon told Willie Geist. “And he goes, ‘No.’ He goes, ‘This movie’s gonna be really hard.’ He, to his credit, was not lying.”

Damon, who also did his own stunts and learned how to use a bow and arrow, shared that the production felt “more like an expedition than a movie,” He added that the entire team, in front of and behind the camera, was “pushed to kind of the limit of what they could do.”
“But the beauty of it is you look around and everyone is going through it with you,” he said.

title: ‘Godzilla vs. Kong’ Actor Kaylee Hottle Dies at 18
summary: Kaylee Hottle, an actor who appeared in two “Godzilla” movies, died at 18 years old in a single-car collision on July 21 in Maryland, according to police and her high school.
story: Kaylee Hottle, an actor who appeared in two “Godzilla” movies, died at 18 years old in a single-car collision on July 21 in Maryland, according to police and her high school.
“It is with profound sadness that we share the heartbreaking news that one of our TSD seniors, Kaylee Hottle, tragically passed away,” the Texas School for the Deaf said in a statement Tuesday.
“Our hearts are with Kaylee’s family, friends, classmates, and everyone who knew and loved her during this incredibly difficult time,” the statement added.

The Texas native played Jia in the 2021 blockbuster “Godzilla vs. Kong,” and again in “Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire” in 2024. She spoke to the Houston Chronicle in 2024 about being a role model as an actor who is deaf.

“I’d like to see more deaf young actresses get motivated when they see me on screen and hopefully they’ll have a chance in Hollywood as well,” she said. “But I just hope that they’ll be inspired, especially deaf people, to be inspired to want to be an actor or actress when they see me on screen.”

Hottle was a passenger in a 1995 Honda Accord being driven by a 19-year-old man when the vehicle traveled off the right side of a two-lane roadway in Ijamsville, Md., and struck a culvert, according to a news release from the Frederick County Sheriff’s Office. Deputies with the sheriff’s office responded to the call at 2:52 a.m. ET on July 21.

Two passengers were in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The driver and another passenger, who were not identified by police, were transported to a local hospital with injuries not believed to be life-threatening, according to the news release.
The second passenger was identified as Hottle, who was transported to an area trauma center and later pronounced dead.
A preliminary investigation found that “excessive speed” is believed to have contributed to the crash, according to the news release. The collision remains under investigation.

Hottle’s father, Joshua Hottle, posted a video on Facebook in which he announced his daughter’s death using American Sign Language. He said that he was flying from his home in Texas to Maryland. It is not clear why his daughter was in Maryland at the time of the crash.
“I am taking a flight that I never would like to take,” he said, according to NBC News affiliate WBAL in Baltimore.

title: Leslie Jones’ Segment Goes Off the Rails as She Hilariously Picks Up Sheinelle
summary: Leslie Jones lifted Sheinelle Jones on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle in a segment that had everybody laughing.
story: A day after Marcello Hernández had Sheinelle Jones in stitches on TODAY, Leslie Jones followed suit.

Jones stopped by TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle on July 21 to chat about her new HGTV series, “Roast My Rental,” in which the former “Saturday Night Live” star gives harsh reviews of low-rated rental properties and then helps renovate them.
To get in the spirit of the show, Jones played a game called “Roast Our Studio,” in which she rated fake flowers, a fake fruit tomato bowl, packaged bagels and the TODAY and NBC logos.
She then roasted TODAY stage manager Dave Auerbach before realizing how much taller she is than Sheinelle, and moving on to that subject.
Jones wrapped her arm around Sheinelle’s shoulder and called her an “oompa loompa” before singing the “oompa loompa” song from “Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory.”
Sheinelle, who is 4-foot-11, then took off her shoes to show her true height, prompting Jones to exclaim, “Girl!”
Sheinelle jumped in the air, at which point Jones picked her up like a husband carrying his new bride over the threshold, while Jenna, Sheinelle and the crew couldn’t hold back their laughter.
“That’s like, ‘I do. I do,’” Sheinelle said, perhaps alluding to the bridal image.
“She is so small,” Jones, who is 6 feet tall, said while peering into the camera before she laughed.
Sheinelle and Jones then swapped high fives as the howling continued while the segment came to an end, with Sheinelle jumping up to reach the comedian’s hands.
“We have lost our mind here in the studio!” Jones said.
You can see Jones do her roasting thing when “Roast My Rental” premieres July 24 at 10 p.m. ET.

title: Costco Esprit Sweatshirt Sells Out After Gen X Staple Goes Viral
summary: Madonna had the No. 1 album in the country, “Little House on the Prairie” is a television hit, and Esprit sweatshirts are sold out.
story: Madonna had the No. 1 album in the country, “Little House on the Prairie” is a television hit, and Esprit sweatshirts are sold out.
What year is it again?
The nostalgia boom has hit the shelves of Costco to the delight of Gen X shoppers, as the pastel-splashed Esprit sweatshirts of ’80s fashion have made a comeback.

The crewneck sweatshirts of the brand Esprit, which is the French word for “spirit,” were a fixture of mall fashion with their bright, stenciled logo. Since being reintroduced by Costco, they have sold out on the company’s website.
Lucky shoppers who have snagged an Esprit sweatshirt at their local Costco have been celebrating the finds online.

“My childhood was unlocked. Look what I found,” TikTok user @heyitsmemamie said in a video on TikTok showing off her new Esprit sweatshirts, one in cream with pastel lettering, one green and one purple. “If you grew up in the ’80s and ’90s, you know that Esprit wasn’t just a brand, it was the brand.”

Esprit was founded in San Francisco by Susie and Doug Tomkins in 1968, but it didn’t become a staple of teen fashion until the 1980s, according to SFGate. The brand ultimately fell on hard times, with its U.S. operations filing for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in 2024. Esprit then announced a business model based on licensing its brand, according to JustStyle.

The coveted Esprit gear at Costco is the latest ’80s- and ’90s-inspired fashion to make a comeback. Gap’s new ’90s inspired jeans collaboration with Hailey Bieber sold out in minutes last week, while Costco has also brought back K-Swiss sneakers.

“It feels good to reconnect with our youth around the age of 40, (or) a little bit older,” nostalgia expert Clay Routledge told NBC News correspondent Joe Fryer on TODAY July 21. “Engaging in this type of nostalgia makes us feel young at heart, so it’s very psychologically beneficial, and it’s also fun.”
The Esprit frenzy also comes after Madonna’s new “Confessions II” album debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard charts, and a rebooted “Little House on the Prairie” became a hit on Netflix.

With cassette mixtapes, VHS tapes and digital cameras also finding a niche with younger audiences as well as Generation X, retailers have found there’s money to be made with a generation that represents about 20% of the U.S. population.

Gen X, which is currently people roughly between the ages of 46 and 61, has control over 30% of household spending and the highest brand loyalty rates of any generation, according to a Nielsen IQ analysis. A study by the consumer research platform GWI also found that Gen X consumers would pay more for a familiar brand.
Plus, nostalgia has become easy to indulge in an age when so much is preserved or revived online.

“The internet and the digital technological platforms that we have today just make it so much easier to share nostalgia,” Routledge said. “People think of nostalgia as this individual thing when in reality it’s a very social experience. People feel nostalgic, and they want to talk to people about their nostalgia.”

title: U.S. launches new strikes and Trump threatens ‘massive attack’ as Iran widens war
summary: The United States launched a fresh barrage of strikes on Iran overnight as President Donald Trump threatened a major new escalation after Tehran opened a second front in its pressure campaign on the world economy.
story: JERUSALEM — The United States launched a fresh barrage of strikes on Iran overnight as President Donald Trump threatened a major new escalation after Tehran opened a second front in its pressure campaign on the world economy.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

Trump was weighing whether to launch a “massive attack” on the Islamic Republic that would be “bigger than ever before,” he told Axios on Thursday. The president’s warning, followed hours later by a 13th night of military strikes, came as oil briefly surged above $100 a barrel.

Iran has shown little sign of bowing to U.S. demands, launching new attacks on shipping, as well as U.S. bases and allies across the Middle East. These have combined to increase the cost of the renewed conflict — in human lives, including American soldiers, and global prices.
The struggle for control of the crucial Strait of Hormuz has now been extended to another key trade route, after attacks by Tehran-backed Houthi rebels in the Red Sea.

And there were signs that some U.S. partners in the region may be losing patience. Senior Arab officials told NBC News they were growing frustrated with the threats, daily escalations and lack of diplomatic progress.

“We have no clue where this is going,” said one senior Arab official, with direct knowledge of regional developments. “It’s only getting crazier,” said another senior Arab official, directly involved with diplomatic efforts.

title: Oil prices surge to $100 per barrel after Red Sea attacks
summary: European and U.S. crude oil both jumped, hitting their highest levels in weeks.
story: Oil prices rose Thursday to their highest levels in nearly two months after the latest Iran war escalation threatened severe new disruptions to global energy supplies.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

Brent crude oil, one of two key global benchmarks, closed higher by 7%, at $100.69 per barrel. Earlier in the trading day, it rose as high as $102 per barrel. That is its highest level in eight weeks, since the end of May.
U.S. crude oil also jumped for a second straight day, closing higher by 6.2%, at $92.19 per barrel — its highest close since June 4.
The prices surged after Tehran-backed Houthi rebels claimed attacks on two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea following their announcement of a naval blockade on the kingdom.
More on Iran war from NBC News

Trump enters an uncertain moment in Iran war that threatens to become a quagmireThat sinking feeling: Iranians feel the strain as Trump ramps up war again over HormuzThe costs of the Iran war are rising as Trump and Tehran signal no letup in the expanding conflict
Trump enters an uncertain moment in Iran war that threatens to become a quagmire
That sinking feeling: Iranians feel the strain as Trump ramps up war again over Hormuz
The costs of the Iran war are rising as Trump and Tehran signal no letup in the expanding conflict
It appeared to be the first time since the Iran war began that ship attacks had spread beyond the vicinity of the Strait of Hormuz, opening up a new front in the volatile conflict.
The Houthi threat is so unsettling to oil markets because millions of barrels per day pass through the Bab el-Mandeb strait to reach global markets.
About 12% to 15% of global maritime trade worth more than $1 trillion transits the waterway every year.
It has also served as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, where traffic remains largely at a standstill, with ship crossings falling to single digits Tuesday.
Since the start of the month, oil prices have now risen about 35%. Those prices are now higher by more than 60% since the start of the year.
Along with oil prices, gas prices have risen, too.
The national average price Thursday rose to $4.09 per gallon, up from $4.06 Wednesday, according to AAA data tracked by NBC News.
That has erased much of the progress toward lower prices after the U.S. and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in mid-June.
That deal has now collapsed, with President Donald Trump threatening Wednesday to blow up an Iranian bridge or power plant for every vessel Tehran attacks.
Then, hours later, came the Houthi claim to have hit two tankers in the Red Sea.

The United Kingdom’s Maritime Trade Office reported a tanker “struck by an unknown projectile” north of the critical Bab el-Mandeb strait in the area. And the state-run Saudi Press Agency reported the Encelia was set ablaze by an attack while it was sailing overnight in the Red Sea, citing an unidentified source from the General Authority of Transport. It did not mention the Layla.

“Inflation has remained top of the agenda for markets this morning,” said Deutsche Bank’s global head of macro research, Jim Reid, citing the jump higher in Brent oil. “Indeed, the strikes between the US and Iran show no sign of easing, and the Houthis said they targeted two oil tankers in the Red Sea yesterday, raising fears that the conflict is widening.”

The worry about inflation as a result of higher oil and gas prices has driven bond yields higher this week. Early Thursday, the U.S. 10-year Treasury bond was trading at 4.7%, its highest level since January 2025.
The 10-year bond has a heavy hand in steering consumer borrowing rates. On Wednesday, the average 30-year U.S. mortgage rate rose to 6.85%, its highest level since July 2025.

Inflation worries and higher oil prices also hit stocks. The S&P 500 fell more than 1.3%, while the Nasdaq slid 2.4%. However, most of the selling came in tech stocks, after Alphabet and Tesla earnings failed to impress investors even though the companies posted generally positive results.

title: ‘Cockroach’ protests spread across India as leading activist ends hunger strike
summary: An activist has ended his 26-day hunger strike that galvanized India’s “Cockroach” protests, turning them into one of the biggest challenges to the government.
story: An activist has ended his 26-day hunger strike that helped to galvanize India’s youth-led “Cockroach” protests, turning them into one of the most sustained challenges to the country’s leadership in years.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

But demonstrators vowed Friday to press on despite Sonam Wangchuk’s decision to end his fast, as the protests spread from New Dehli to other cities around the country including Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Ahmedabad.

Wangchuk’s fast began amid protests for education reforms after alleged leaks in some of the country’s most competitive university entrance exams, but quickly became a lightning rod for public anger over education, economic inequality and the rule of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Wangchuk said in a post on X that he ended his fast after appeals from dozens of members of Parliament and following “a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country.” Conceding that not all his demands were met, he said two federal lawmakers were present when he finished.
However, Abhijeet Dipke, a Boston University graduate and founder of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), said the protests will continue until India’s Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns.

“After all of this, we don’t accept anything less than a resignation,” he told supporters on Friday as protests showed no sign of dying down. CJP leaders have said they started talks with government officials at a neutral venue, raising hopes of a breakthrough in the standoff.

The CJP began as a satirical youth political movement after India’s Chief Justice Surya Kant compared unemployed young people to “cockroaches.” But the movement has soared in popularity and mounted the biggest challenge to Modi in his 12 years in power.
On Thursday night, Modi offered his first public comments, posting a video on Instagram addressing the young protesters and concerns about the exam paper leaks.
“I know the paper leak is not a trivial matter,” he said in his video. He also defended his government’s decision to let 2 million students retake medical entrance exams.
He also announced fast-track courts would prosecute cases involving examination paper leaks.

But protesters said his response fell short of their demands for accountability and hundreds of people returned to the streets of New Delhi on Friday even as authorities shut 18 stations the city’s metro network, disrupting a vital mode of transportation for its 23 million residents.

title: Trump says Saudi Arabia must normalize Israel ties before nuclear deal is approved
summary: The president added that the deal “is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords.”
story: President Donald Trump said Thursday that a nuclear deal between the United States and Saudi Arabia requires the kingdom to normalize relations with Israel — a significant condition not previously mentioned as the deal was announced.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

There will ⁠be “​no ⁠enrichment of ⁠material” under the agreement, he wrote on Truth Social, adding that the deal signed a day earlier “pertains only to non-military use.” Lawmakers and experts have raised concerns that the civil nuclear agreement could fuel nuclear proliferation in the Middle East.
Trump added that the deal “is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords.”

The U.S.-brokered agreements aimed at normalizing relations with Israel were forged during Trump’s first term and signed by several majority-Muslim countries including the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain, and later Sudan and Morocco. Their expansion across the Middle East has been a long-standing objective for Trump in his second term.

An agreement to normalize ties between Israel and Saudi Arabia had previously been a U.S. requirement for any deal allowing the Gulf kingdom to enrich uranium, but Saudi leaders have long insisted that would not be possible without meaningful progress toward a Palestinian state.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has dismissed the idea of Palestinian statehood, but his office said in a statement that Saudi Arabia joining the Abraham Accords “would be an historic leap forward for peace in the Middle East.”

The Energy Department said Wednesday that the agreements “lay the legal foundation for a decades-long, multi-billion-dollar partnership that advances several priority economic and strategic objectives, including nuclear nonproliferation.”
A senior administration official told NBC News on Wednesday that Trump had approved the deal, which was expected to be submitted to Congress for review.

It was not expected to require the most rigorous level of United Nations inspections or include a ban on uranium enrichment or reprocessing of spent nuclear fuel, according to three people familiar with the agreement. They said the pact would allow U.S. companies to build a uranium enrichment facility in Saudi Arabia pending a joint U.S.-Saudi study examining whether such a step would be feasible.

Critics and nonproliferation groups have warned that such a deal could further the development of nuclear weapons in the region at a time when one of Trump’s stated aims for the Iran war is preventing Tehran from developing one.

While Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has said nuclear weapons are not his country’s aim, in a 2018 interview with CBS News he said: “Without a doubt if Iran developed a nuclear bomb, we will follow suit as soon as possible.”

There was no mention of the Abraham Accords when the Energy Department announced the deal on X on Wednesday, although the text of the deal was not released, and the Trump administration has not publicly outlined its details.
It was signed by Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman.

The oil-rich kingdom did not mention Trump’s stipulations in its own release about the agreement, which said the deal would attempt to “diversify energy sources, advance cutting-edge technologies, and expand opportunities for cooperation and investment in ways that serve the mutual interests of the two friendly countries.”

Saudi Arabia is a member state of the International Atomic Energy Agency, which promotes peaceful nuclear work but also inspects nations to ensure they do not have clandestine atomic weapons programs. Based in Vienna, the agency reports to the U.N. General Assembly and Security Council.
Nuclear enrichment is part of the process of both civil nuclear power generation and, at higher grades of enrichment, the development of nuclear weapons.

title: U.S. signs landmark nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia
summary: The U.S. will support creating a civilian nuclear power program in the kingdom under the agreement, a senior administration official told NBC News.
story: The U.S. signed a landmark nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, the Energy Department announced on X.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

“U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright and Saudi Minister of Energy His Royal Highness (HRH) Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman signed a peaceful nuclear cooperation agreement, commonly known as a 123 agreement, alongside an accompanying bilateral safeguards agreement,” the announcement read. “Together, these two agreements lay the legal foundation for a decades-long, multi-billion-dollar partnership that advances several priority economic and strategic objectives, including nuclear nonproliferation.”

In the announcement, Wright added: “Rest assured, these agreements uphold the highest standards of nuclear safety and nonproliferation, while relying on the world’s best nuclear technology and scientists, designed right here in the United States.”
Earlier, a senior administration official told NBC News that President Donald Trump had approved the deal.

The U.S. will support creating a nuclear power program and American companies will build the program in the kingdom under the agreement, said the official, who was granted anonymity to speak about the deal before its official announcement.

The deal is not expected to require the most rigorous level of U.N. inspections or include a ban on uranium enrichment or reprocessing of spent nuclear fuel, according to three people familiar with the agreement.

The pact would allow U.S. companies to build a uranium enrichment facility in Saudi Arabia pending a joint U.S.-Saudi study examining whether such a step would be feasible, the people said. The text of the deal has not been released, and the administration has not publicly outlined its details.
The Wall Street Journal first reported news of the agreement.

Congress will be required to vote on the agreement but would need a veto-proof majority to actually block it, which could pave the way for the kingdom to pursue its own uranium enrichment and would be likely to raise fears of nuclear proliferation.

Asked ahead of the announcement about those concerns and reports of an expected deal, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that the U.S. would not “reach any agreement with any country in the world that leads to the risk of proliferation.”

The agreement comes as the war against Iran that the U.S. and Israel launched in late February goes on. Trump has insisted that Tehran should not be able to develop a nuclear weapon, even as the Islamic Republic consistently denies it plans to do so.

An agreement to normalize ties between Israel and Saudi Arabia had been a U.S. requirement for any deal allowing the kingdom to enrich uranium, but Saudi leaders insisted that would not be possible without meaningful progress toward a Palestinian state.

However, Wright discussed building the country’s commercial nuclear power industry with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman Al Saud, on a visit to the kingdom last year, shortly before Trump traveled there himself in May 2025.

Any deal without appropriate guardrails would be “concerning from a proliferation perspective,” said Darya Dolzikova​, a senior research fellow with the proliferation and nuclear policy program at the Royal United Services Institute, a London-based think tank.
“Any country, period, but particularly countries of proliferation concern have to be really, really robust on their nonproliferation provisions,” she added.
And Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has warned that the kingdom would try to obtain a nuclear weapon if Iran were also able to, Dolzikova​ noted.

Saudi Arabia also signed a mutual defense pact with Pakistan, the only Muslim nuclear nation, in September. Pakistani Defense Minister Khawaja Asif then said his country’s nuclear program would “be made available” to Saudi Arabia if required.

Saudi Arabia is a member state of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), which promotes peaceful nuclear work but also inspects nations to ensure they do not have clandestine atomic weapon programs. Based in Vienna, the agency reports to the United Nations General Assembly and Security Council.

While enrichment does not necessarily lead to a nuclear weapon, it can open the door to it. However, any country wishing to pursue one would also have to master other technologies, including the use of synchronized high explosives.

And there has been focus on whether any deal would include the “gold standard” safeguards that would block Saudi Arabia from enriching uranium and reprocessing spent nuclear fuel, both of which are potential pathways to nuclear weapons.
It also remains to be seen whether the agreement includes the “Additional Protocol” that grants the IAEA greater oversight of a country’s nuclear activities.

Ultimately, “the devil will be in the details,” said Sanam Vakil, director of the Middle East and North Africa program at the London-based think tank Chatham House. If Saudi Arabia does retain the right to enrich, she said, “it’s the issue of domestic enrichment that will be more concerning and alarming.”

The deal with the U.S. came a day after senior Saudi and United Arab Emirates officials shared similar social media posts ​affirming their close historical ties and “wise leadership,” a move that follows months of tensions owing to a rift ‌between the two Persian Gulf monarchies.

The Gulf nations have been divided over ​their support for opposing sides in the war in Yemen, which culminated in a Saudi airstrike late last year on what it said was a shipment of UAE military equipment to the Yemeni faction Abu Dhabi backed.
Their interests have diverged over a number of issues, including oil quotas.
But the posts from Saudi Media Minister Salman Al-Dosary and Abdulla bin Mohamed Alhamed, chairman of the UAE National Media Authority, said they should focus on their shared history and heritage.

title: U.S. military identifies soldiers killed in Iranian attack in Jordan
summary: The Pentagon identified the soldiers as 25-year-old Tyler James Feehan of Hawaii and 19-year-old Isabella Gonzales of Texas.
story: The Defense Department on Monday released the names of two soldiers killed in Iranian strikes in Jordan, identifying them as 25-year-old Tyler James Feehan of Hawaii and 19-year-old Isabella Gonzales of Texas.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.
Gonzales was killed Friday and Feehan on Saturday. The Pentagon did not provide details on the exact circumstances of their deaths.
Feehan and Gonzales had been assigned to Army missile defense commands in Fort Bragg, North Carolina, and Ansbach, Germany, respectively, it said.
The Pentagon said they were part of a longtime, ongoing mission to counter ISIS, Operation Inherent Resolve, that began in 2014.

The service members were not technically part of the war with Iran, dubbed Operation Epic Fury by the Pentagon, despite President Donald Trump saying Sunday that they were killed while ensuring Iran does not get a nuclear weapon.
“Those great patriots were out there fighting that Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon,” Trump told reporters.
In addition, another U.S. service member was killed in a separate incident in Iraq.

The release of the two soldiers’ identities comes after the U.S. military announced Sunday that it had recovered unidentified human remains while searching for an American service member reported missing following an Iranian missile and drone attack in Jordan.

U.S. Central Command said military personnel found the remains Sunday at the site of Friday’s attack in Jordan. Officials said an examination is underway to determine whether they belong to the missing service member.
On Tuesday, the Pentagon announced the “believed to be death of an active-duty Soldier who was supporting overseas operations in Jordan” in a statement.

“Sgt. Angel S. Rampersad, 28, of Ozone Park, New York, is believed to have been killed in action on July 17, 2026, during an enemy attack at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, Jordan. The incident is under investigation. U.S. Central Command previously announced this Soldier as missing. The Soldier status was updated to a Duty Status–Whereabouts Unknown and is believed to be deceased,” the statement said.
Central Command said Saturday that two service members were killed and a third was missing following Iran’s attack Friday on U.S. and partner forces in Jordan.

Separately, a U.S. service member was killed Saturday in northern Iraq during the controlled detonation of unexploded ordnance from a downed Iranian one-way attack drone, the combatant command said. A second service member suffered a minor injury and remains under medical care.
“Our hearts go out to these families,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters Sunday. “These are heroes that pay the ultimate price.”

In a social media post Monday, Trump said U.S. military leaders had been given the directive to make Iran pay “many times over” for the killing of U.S. soldiers. White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said Monday afternoon in a post on X that the president would attend the transfer of the remains of the service members at Dover Air Force Base in Delaware on Tuesday night.
Leavitt later posted on X that the transfer of remains would not take place Tuesday. “The exact day and time are still being finalized,” she wrote.

Fifteen U.S. service members have been killed in combat since military operations against Iran began, while two more service members died from noncombat-related causes. American military members who have been wounded since the start of the conflict now number 140, including eight who were wounded severely.
The discrepancy in the naming of the conflict reflects an ongoing confusion about the war with Iran — specifically about whether Operation Epic Fury continues.

NBC News previously reported that the Trump administration was considering renaming the start of combat operations in Iran to circumvent the 1973 War Powers Resolution, which requires troops to be withdrawn within 60 days of starting combat operations if Congress was not notified beforehand.
In May, Trump notified Congress that Operation Epic Fury had ended. Since then, the Pentagon has not said what the ongoing military operation in Iran is named.

The military says Operation Inherent Resolve is the Combined Joint Task Force that works with partner forces to ensure the defeat of the Islamic State militant group. Asked about the discrepancy in the mission the fallen service members were on, acting Pentagon press secretary Joel Valdez said in a statement, “They were deployed on orders to support Operation Inherent Resolve.”

There are more than 50,000 troops in the region, according to U.S. Central Command. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Dan Caine last gave a briefing at the Pentagon on the Iran war in May.
At least 3,375 people have been killed in Iran since military operations began, according to the country’s state-affiliated news media, citing a senior judicial official.

The mounting death toll has effectively ended the interim ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran negotiated last month. After weeks of trading accusations that each side has violated the agreement, the two countries resumed attacks, with U.S. forces striking Iranian military targets and Tehran launching missiles and drones at U.S. allies in the region.
Rubio said that the U.S. remained open to diplomacy with Iran, but that “even within their own system, there’s a growing split.”

“They continue to send signals that they want to talk, that they want to negotiate,” he said. “But their behavior is what we’re responding to, and their behavior is they’re launching missiles and drones against ships, including tonight.”
“Their behavior has to change in order for ours to change,” Rubio added.

On Sunday evening, Central Command said it conducted a ninth consecutive night of attacks on Iran starting at 7 p.m. ET. It said in a subsequent statement shortly after 10 p.m. ET that the strikes had concluded.

“CENTCOM assets targeted Iranian military command centers, air defense and coastal surveillance sites, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites, and communications networks to further diminish Iran’s ability to attack commercial vessels and civilian mariners transiting the Strait of Hormuz,” it said.

On Saturday, the command said U.S. forces completed the eighth night of launching munitions against Iran when it targeted Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces believed to have been involved in Friday’s attack on U.S. service members in Jordan.

The military said the two service members died defending against an Iranian ballistic missile and drone attack. Four other U.S. service members were medically evacuated to hospitals in Jordan and have since been discharged.

title: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy fires his commander in chief after protests and major rift
summary: The firing caps a crisis for Volodymyr Zelenskyy after Ukrainians took to the streets to call for Oleksandr Syrskyi’s resignation.
story: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy fired his commander in chief, Oleksandr Syrskyi, on Tuesday, bowing to pressure after the removal of popular Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov sparked the fiercest leadership crisis of his presidency.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.
Zelenskyy announced on Telegram that Mykhailo Drapatyi will replace Syrskyi.

Zelenskyy’s decision to fire Fedorov, one of his closest allies, led to rare wartime protests on the streets of Kyiv. Fedorov publicly aired his disagreements with Syrskyi, known as “The Butcher,” over military strategy.

Syrskyi, 60, is a more traditional military commander focused on infantry and artillery, while Fedorov, 35, is seen as a modernizer, whose focus on technological advancements in drone warfare has led to Ukraine’s recent successes in hitting Russia.
Despite the recent shake-up, Zelenskyy tried to present a unified front in his Telegram message Tuesday announcing the dismissal of Syrskyi.
“The desire in all of us is one — victory over the enemy and achieving such conditions on the front and in pressure on Russia, which would allow forcing Russia to peace,” he wrote.

Worried Ukrainians, fearing that Fedorov’s removal could wipe out recent gains, had taken to the streets calling for him to be reinstated and Syrskyi to be forced out, instead. A senior air force commander also quit in protest.

For those in the streets, Syrskyi had become a symbol of the Soviet way of thinking rejected by Ukraine’s younger generations. Fedorov, meanwhile, represents technological innovation and a determination to outsmart the country’s more powerful invader.

Syrskyi has been nicknamed “The Butcher” for his unsparing reputation, with critics pointing to lives lost in a late withdrawal from the fortress city of Bakhmut and the disastrous retreat from Russia’s Kursk region last year that left soldiers stranded and forced to walk back for days under enemy fire.

Zelenskyy spent the weekend speaking to other top military commanders in an apparent interview process to potentially replace Syrskyi. It is unclear whether Fedorov will remain in the government and, if so, in what capacity.

On Tuesday, Zelenskyy separately met with Fedorov and offered him what he called a respected position in government that would unify the country’s technology sector. But it was not clear whether Fedorov accepted the offer and whether the latest moves would satisfy protesters and bring peace to the streets.
“Change is inevitable,” Fedorov said Saturday on social media. “The dialogue is happening. I believe we will succeed.”

Zelenskyy did not give a reason for firing Fedorov last week. He said he was effectively left with a choice between the defense minister and Syrskyi, who was heading the armed forces. The two were no longer communicating with each other, he said.
Fedorov confirmed his spat with Syrskyi, saying Syrskyi was not willing to discuss “problems” directly and resisted reform of Ukraine’s defense apparatus.
Protests erupt in Ukraine over defense minister's ouster
While he credited Syrskyi for Ukraine’s wins in the early days of the war, “the war has changed” because of drone advancements, Fedorov argued.
“Why is this trajectory breaking now, and why are we veering off course? There is such a risk. And the Ukrainian people have taken to the streets for that,” he said at a news conference.

Ukraine’s deployment of low-cost drones has upended the battlefield and the traditional model of warfare, with Kyiv demonstrating a growing ability to hit strategic sites deep inside Russia, in addition to critical Russian-held targets within Ukraine’s territory.

At the same time, Russian troops continue to slowly advance in eastern Ukraine, while a dwindling supply of missile interceptors has left Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities vulnerable to intense bombardment.

title: Andy Burnham becomes seventh British prime minister in a decade
summary: The new Labour Party leader, Andy Burnham, replaced Keir Starmer as British prime minister, inheriting a country beset by low wages and internal strife.
story: LONDON — Over to you, Andy Burnham.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

The man dubbed the “King of the North” became the new British prime minister Monday, the latest in a revolving door of leaders trying to halt a decade of political turbulence and economic stagnation in the United Kingdom.
Burnham, 56, was appointed unchallenged after the unpopular Keir Starmer agreed to step down last month following a series of election defeats, U-turns and scandals.

Both Starmer and Burnham come from the same center-left Labour Party, and in the United Kingdom ruling parties can change leaders — and therefore the prime minister — in the middle of an election cycle without anyone voting.
That said, Burnham has promised radical change after taking office following a morning of royal formality, though he already faces infighting over his Cabinet selections.

Burnham reappointed ‌Shabana Mahmood as ​interior ‌minister, but he moved several members of Starmer’s team out of their roles. Former Labour leader Ed Miliband was appointed as foreign minister in place of Yvette Cooper and John Healey became finance minister.
Healey, the former defense minister, helped to trigger the departure of Starmer by accusing him of failing to spend enough money on keeping the country safe.
Making his first speech as prime minister outside No. 10 Downing St., Burnham vowed a “circuit breaker for Britain” that would involve “the biggest changes of the past 40 years.”
In keeping with the more casual style he’s sought to project, Burnham eschewed the lectern favored by his predecessors, instead speaking while standing freely in the famous street.

He said that later this year he would announce a “10-year plan” for Britain, but also that he would be doing things “to give people some breathing space now,” including “some help with the cost of living,” he said. His first “instruction,” Burnham said, would be to “end rough sleeping in our country.”
He said, “I know people at home are fed up with politics. I hear you and I want to be honest with you — we have not been good enough and we need to be better.”
President Donald Trump said he a good call with Burnham on Monday and noted that they would be meeting in the “not too distant future.”

“I had a very good conversation with the new Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, Andy Burnham. We discussed many subjects, including the outstanding relationship we have had with the UK. We will be meeting in the not too distant future for topics of mutual interest,” Trump wrote in a post on X. “The Prime Minister has got a big job ahead of him, but he will be able to do it and, of course, the U.S.A. will be there to help! We discussed North Sea Oil, Trade, the Military Alliance, Demining of the Hormuz Strait, and many other topics. The call was interesting, and went very well. I wished Prime Minister Burnham, GOOD LUCK AND GODSPEED!”

The incoming leader has a heaving inbox: how to solve Britain’s cost-of-living crisis, revive its ailing National Health Service, and navigate bitter debates over immigration and Europe. He must also fend off the challenge from Reform UK, the hard-right party led by Trump ally Nigel Farage, which tops the polls.

title: Tate brothers arrested by U.S. authorities, face additional rape charges in the U.K.
summary: Social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate were taken into custody by federal law enforcement officials in Miami on Saturday, the U.S.
story: Social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate were taken into custody by federal law enforcement officials in Miami on Saturday, the U.S. Marshals Service said, in arrests British authorities said were related to additional charges of rape.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.
“We can confirm the arrest of the Tate brothers today in Miami,” it stated. “The warrant was sealed so we are unable to confirm the charges.”

The U.K.’s Crown Prosecution Service said it is bringing additional charges of rape against Andrew, 39, and Tristan, 38, under ongoing cases against the brothers in that nation. The agency said the brothers are awaiting extradition to the U.K.

Andrew Tate faces seven additional counts of rape, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and 19 additional charges relating to illegal child images and pornography, the Crown Prosecution Service said.
Tristan Tate faces one count of sexual assault, two counts of rape and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, it said.
The allegations cover alleged offenses from July 2010 to August 2017, the service said.

Malcolm McHaffie, head of the Special Crime Division at the Crown Prosecution Service, said in a statement that the charges come after the agency received a new file of evidence from the Bedfordshire Police force.
The new charges relate to four additional alleged victims; previous charges were connected to three alleged victims.
The case against Tristan previously included three counts of rape, six counts of actual bodily harm and two counts of human trafficking.
Tate’s case previously included three counts of rape, four counts of actual bodily harm, two counts of human trafficking and one count of controlling prostitution for gain.
Assistant Chief Constable Karena Thomas of Bedfordshire Police said the complex investigation involved cooperation between “national and international law enforcement agencies.”
She added: “There is no place for male violence against women and girls, and we will continue to work tirelessly to support victims and investigate all reports made to us.”

Joseph D. McBride, a New York City attorney who has been representing the pair in civil litigation, said Saturday that the arrests were an “egregious abuse” of authority by federal officials in the United States.
He said U.K. authorities “conjured up a wave of charges against the Tate brothers” and he predicted the pair would “walk free” before traveling across the Atlantic.
“This is not law enforcement,” he said. “This is a political hit. ... America does not do Britain’s political dirty work.”

On Sunday, McBride said on X that he visited the brothers on Sunday and found them in solitary confinement as they await extradition proceedings. McBride described them as “political prisoners” and “two innocent men, charged with nothing in America, dressed like enemy combatants.”

The brothers, both former kickboxers, are often associated with  the “manosphere,” a social media movement that seeks to elevate men and invalidate feminism, and they have been accused of embodying toxic masculinity and misogyny.
They are dual U.S. and British citizens and moved to Romania in 2016, but amid a criminal investigation there, they returned to the United States last year.
The two have not been convicted of any of the crimes alleged by U.K. or Romanian authorities and have steadfastly denied committing the alleged crimes.

They were arrested along with two Romanian women in Bucharest in 2022 and subsequently indicted. A representative said last year that a Romanian travel ban on the two was lifted, allowing them to return to the United States.

Their return took place in early 2025 as they remained under criminal investigation in Romania on allegations of organized crime, human trafficking, trafficking minors and money laundering. They have denied any wrongdoing.
Speaking last year, attorney McBride said the two planned to travel to Romania to meet with prosecutors there before returning to the U.S.

title: U.S. and Iran trade strikes after two U.S. service members killed in Jordan
summary: Two U.S. service members were killed Friday while defending against an Iranian ballistic missile and drone attack in Jordan, and another service member is missing, U.S.
story: Two U.S. service members were killed Friday while defending against an Iranian ballistic missile and drone attack in Jordan, and another service member is missing, U.S. Central Command said Saturday.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

Central Command, known as CENTCOM, said the troops were killed in action as U.S. and partner forces responded to the attack. It did not specify where in Jordan the attack occurred or provide additional details about the circumstances.

Four other American service members were medically evacuated to hospitals in Jordan but have since been discharged, CENTCOM said. Other personnel who were evaluated for minor injuries have returned to duty.
CENTCOM said it was withholding the identities of the two service members killed until 24 hours after their families have been notified.
The U.S. launched retaliatory airstrikes on Saturday at President Donald Trump’s direction in order to “swiftly punish” Iranian forces for the attack, CENTCOM said in a statement.

CENTCOM said that the strikes were also intended to weaken Iran’s “ability to threaten commercial shipping” in the Strait of Hormuz, the latest move by the U.S. to pressure Tehran to give up its control of the critical trade route.

Late Saturday, CENTCOM said U.S. forces completed the eighth consecutive night of launching munitions against Iran, including Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces believed to have targeted U.S. service members in Jordan on Friday.
It said U.S. forces struck Iranian military surveillance and air defense facilities, maritime assets and missile and drone storage sites.
The International Atomic Energy Agency said on Sunday that it was investigating reports of an overnight attack on the construction site of Iran’s planned Darkhovin nuclear power plant.

Iran’s semiofficial news agency Tasnim said on Telegram overnight that its own forces had launched “massive drone attacks” on key U.S. military sites in Kuwait and that its attacks would impact U.S. military support operations in the Middle East.
Kuwait’s army said Sunday that its air defenses were “confronting hostile missile and drone attacks.”
The country’s electricity ministry said on X that Iran had attacked a power and water desalination plant twice in two days, causing a fire in part of the facility.

Bahrain, which hosts the U.S. Navy’s 5th Fleet, said Sunday that its air defenses had intercepted an Iranian attack. Its interior ministry said on X that citizens and residents should “remain calm and head to the nearest safe place.”
Jordan’s army forces said it shot down three Iranian missiles targeting the kingdom, according to state television.

The attack that killed U.S. forces comes as the conflict between the U.S. and Iran has intensified following the collapse of an interim ceasefire. The two countries have traded daily strikes over the past week, with Iran launching ballistic missiles and drones at U.S. military positions and American allies across the region, including Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain, while U.S. forces have carried out repeated strikes on Iranian military targets.

Jordan said earlier Saturday that its forces intercepted Iranian missiles and drones that Tehran said were aimed at an American military base in the country. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed at least two U.S. fighter jets were destroyed in the attack, according to Iran’s Tasnim news agency. NBC News has not independently verified that claim.
